queue.title: How can Chinese intelligent driving capabilities enter global vehicle development?
queue.text:
Gasgoo Munich-
On September 24, Dongfeng Stellantis Automotive Technology (Wuhan) Co., Ltd. (
"
DSAT
"
) and Momenta announced a global strategic partnership. The companies plan to jointly develop advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), based on Momenta
'
s R7 World Model, for new Peugeot and Jeep
®
production models, with China, Europe and other global markets in scope.

Viewed solely as an ADAS supplier award, the agreement risks being understated. Momenta is not entering a vehicle programme designed only for China; it is joining the global development path for new Peugeot and Jeep
®
products. For DSAT, the task is not simply to add another intelligent function to a new vehicle, but to bring Chinese intelligent-driving technology into product development across brands and markets.

That makes the partnership a case worth watching for China
'
s intelligent-driving sector: whether mass-production experience developed in China can enter the global vehicle programmes of established international brands, and then meet the tests of different regulations, roads and user expectations.

[IMG:0]

Image source: Momenta

## From China-specific products to global vehicle programmes

DSAT General Manager Lü Haitao described the agreement as the company
'
s first strategic, technology-focused partnership since its establishment. In his view, the transition to new energy vehicles has created a new product foundation for joint-venture brands, but intelligent-driving technology is evolving too quickly for companies to remain in a catch-up position.

"We do not want simply to fill an intelligent-driving gap in the Chinese market,"
Mr.
Lü said. "We want Chinese intelligent-driving capabilities to go global with the vehicles."

[IMG:1]

Lü Haitao, General Manager of DSAT

The shift lies in where the technology enters the development process.

Historically, when international-brand models entered China, configuration, functions and user experience were often adapted locally. Under this partnership, ADAS capabilities are intended to be introduced earlier, at the product-definition and development stages, before new Peugeot and Jeep
®
models are advanced for multiple markets. Chinese technology would therefore need to contribute not only to China-specific intelligent functions, but also to engineering integration and vehicle delivery for global programmes.

Momenta CEO Cao Xudong described the cooperation as involving two "zero-to-one" transitions. The first concerns building intelligent-driving capabilities for joint-venture brands such as Peugeot and Jeep
®
. The second is an "in China, for the world" model for taking that capability overseas.

The first is more than the addition of an ADAS feature. For brands with established design languages, driving characteristics and usage scenarios, intelligent-driving functions need to be considered from the product-definition stage: which users they are intended to serve, where they should intervene and how they should work with the overall vehicle experience.

The second changes the route through which the technology enters a vehicle. Intelligent-driving solutions have largely been developed around vehicles and user needs in the Chinese market. In this case, Momenta
'
s R7 World Model is planned to support ADAS development for new Peugeot and Jeep
®
production models intended for China, Europe and other global markets. Algorithms, mass-production know-how and scenario experience accumulated in China would enter global vehicle development earlier, before being tested against the regulatory, road, user and product requirements of different markets.

Neither of Cao
'
s "zero-to-one" transitions can replace the other. Adding intelligent-driving capability does not automatically give a vehicle global adaptability, while access to global markets does not ensure that the technology will express a brand
'
s character consistently. The partnership is an attempt to build coordination between brand products, intelligent-driving capability and global vehicle development.

## Why Momenta needs a global vehicle path

For Momenta, the value of working with DSAT extends beyond the addition of another vehicle programme.

Momenta says it has established partnerships with global top-10 automakers and now works with 26 OEMs in total. Co-developing advanced driver-assistance systems with international brands is becoming one route in its global expansion. The Peugeot and Jeep
®
programmes are distinct because the cooperation begins at the product-definition stage and is intended to accompany new vehicles into China, Europe and other markets.

The company will therefore need to demonstrate more than whether its system can operate overseas. It will also need to show that its technology can fit the development cadence, product requirements and global delivery standards of international-brand vehicles.

Cao believes China's intelligent-driving market is around four years ahead of global markets. He said the inflection point for urban navigation-on-autopilot systems may have emerged in China in 2024, while a comparable window for global markets could arrive around 2028. Momenta hopes to complete its preparations "at least half a step early" before that point, he said, giving it an opportunity to compete globally.

Participation in global vehicle development does not mean Momenta is starting from zero in mass-production experience. The company says its systems have been installed in more than 1.2 million production vehicles and have accumulated more than 17 billion kilometres of real-world driving, alongside training and simulation data.

Those capabilities provide a foundation for its involvement in the development of new Peugeot and Jeep
®
models. Yet whether its existing mass-production experience can become stable, cross-market product capability will still depend on subsequent development and delivery, as systems encounter different road environments, regulatory requirements and user habits.

## One technology should not produce the same vehicle

Entering global vehicle programmes does not mean copying a single system across markets and brands.

Peugeot and Jeep
®
have different product priorities. Peugeot places emphasis on design and driving dynamics, while Jeep
®
has a distinct off-road use case and product identity. A standardised ADAS solution may be able to deliver its functions across different vehicles, but that alone would not ensure that customers experience the brands differently.

The two companies have therefore proposed a model of jointly defining products. Cao said vehicle competitiveness begins with defining the brand and product around the user, then translating that definition into specific scenarios and identifying the distinct value that intelligent driving can provide.

DSAT is expected to define vehicle-level and scenario requirements, while Momenta will participate in development around its world-model and intelligent-driving capabilities. The teams also plan to coordinate the system with steering, suspension and chassis control, adapting it for scenarios including commuter traffic, stop-and-go driving, narrow urban roads, highway driving, complex parking situations and control on unpaved surfaces.

Lü described the role of an automaker as that of an "integrator." A single system may be technically capable, he said, but that does not guarantee the best overall vehicle experience. The automaker must bring together ADAS, cockpit functions, chassis systems and hardware into a complete product.

The central question for this cooperation is therefore whether Momenta's R7 World Model can retain a common technical base across products while being expressed differently through Peugeot's driving dynamics and Jeep
®
's off-road character.

## Globalization is more than taking a system overseas

Ultimately, "in China, for the world" must translate into global product delivery.

Cao said Momenta began preparing overseas data, infrastructure, teams and regulatory adaptation in 2021. If the jointly developed vehicles enter more markets, differences in road environments, driving habits and user needs will become further variables for continued system adaptation.

[IMG:2]

Cao Xudong, Momenta CEO

This is the practical test for a world-model approach. Road rules, certification requirements, data obligations, user habits and cost structures vary by market. Whether a common technology base can iterate across markets depends not only on the model itself, but also on the coordination of vehicle development, certification, data compliance and product delivery.

Lü noted that joint ventures and Chinese automakers have traditionally developed products around individual markets. Developing vehicles for global markets requires companies to coordinate different certification regimes, road scenarios, user needs, cost requirements and product standards. North America, he added, has a relatively distinct system of its own.

For that reason, global capability needs to be built during vehicle development rather than added once a product is ready to enter overseas markets. DSAT and Momenta are seeking to embed intelligent-driving experience accumulated in China earlier in the global development process for international brands, then test whether the collaboration can become a deliverable product capability through subsequent vehicle and market validation.

The next questions extend beyond when the first models will arrive. Can ADAS be meaningfully integrated with the product experiences associated with Peugeot and Jeep
®
? Can the systems meet regulatory and scenario requirements across markets? And can global vehicle delivery, in turn, generate new data and product iteration?

If those links can be established, the partnership may offer a useful reference point for how Chinese intelligent-driving technology can move beyond domestic vehicle programmes and enter a broader global automotive value chain.

Always up to date. Here you can find all press materials for Automechanika Shanghai.

As automotive companies navigate evolving market dynamics, business expansion requires an ecosystem-driven approach whereby entire networks move into new spaces, including market segments and geographical locations. This is particularly noticeable in China’s commercial vehicle sector as electrification grows across the market segment. Automechanika Shanghai brings these trends to light, enabling players to connect and strategise opportunities both at home and abroad. The fair will converge 7,600 exhibitors from 2 to 5 December at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) covering passenger and commercial vehicles with various powertrains.

The 21st edition of Automechanika Shanghai will continue to champion the transformation of the automotive industry. Held at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) from 2 to 5 December 2026, the show will occupy the entire venue, including 390,000 sqm across 16 halls and mezzanine floor to host an anticipated 7,600 exhibitors. In line with the latest global and domestic automotive trends, the show will comprehensively highlight three core themes: technological innovation, product evolution, and service enhancement. By integrating the extensive exhibition platform with a highly impactful conference programme, Automechanika Shanghai 2026 offers comprehensive resources for the automotive industry and its ever-growing ecosystem.

Automechanika Shanghai 2025 concludes successfully on 29 November, leaving a lasting impression marked by record-breaking participation from visitors and exhibitors. Across four days, the fair celebrated the innovative advancement of the automotive supply chain, offering a sustainable outlook of how the industry is coming together for the development and upgrade of various vehicle types; a particularly important standpoint given these markets represented at the show have different needs. Participants praised the wide array of product showcases, opportunities presented for networking at fringe programme events, and high level of training at the specialised areas.

Automechanika Shanghai has once again set new benchmarks, concluding its latest edition with record-breaking participation that captured the attention of the global automotive community. From 26 to 29 November 2025, the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) came alive with 253,691 visitors eager to connect with 7,465 exhibitors. This year’s event was not just about numbers; it showcased a strong commitment to fostering supply chain collaboration, aligning with industry trends, and nurturing the next generation of talent.

Automechanika Shanghai 2025 opens tomorrow with a record 7,465 exhibitors (10 percent increase), from 44 countries and regions reflecting a strong commitment to innovation and sustainability in the automotive industry. The exhibition spans 383,000 sqm (nine percent increase); it marks the first time all 15 halls of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) are utilised. With 15 country and region pavilions and a presence from key manufacturing hubs across China, the show delivers a global platform for marketing, trade, information exchange, and education. Activities begin today with the International Automotive Industry Conference 2025 Presented by Automechanika Shanghai – CEO Summit, bringing together executives from around the world to discuss the current and future automotive industry, a reflection of what to expect across the next four days.

Gavin Newsom to enact Senate Bill 719 before a technically unworkable state requirement takes effect July 1 and potentially forces the suspension of new and used vehicle sales in California. Alliance
queue.text:
Bill preserves protections for domestic violence survivors while replacing technically impossible deadlines with a workable implementation schedule

SACRAMENTO, CA
— Alliance for Automotive Innovation today urged the California Legislature and Gov. Gavin Newsom to enact Senate Bill 719 before a technically unworkable state requirement takes effect July 1 and potentially forces the suspension of new and used vehicle sales in California.

SB 719, authored by Sen. Christopher Cabaldon, updates the implementation schedule for vehicle technologies required under SB 1394, legislation enacted in 2024 to prevent perpetrators of domestic violence from using connected vehicle services to track, monitor or harass survivors.

“Without SB 719 being signed into law before July 1, there is substantial risk that auto sales in California will be suspended,”
said Curt Augustine, senior director of state affairs at Alliance for Automotive Innovation
. “Automakers are already implementing the domestic violence victim protections required by SB 1394, but compliance with some elements of the law is impossible this year. The additional year provided by SB 719 merely aligns implementation with the reality of vehicle design and manufacturing.”

Despite the bill’s unanimous legislative support to date, last-minute opposition threatens to prevent its enactment before the July 1 deadline.

“Passage of Sen. Cabaldon’s bill is being complicated by last-minute opposition and misinformation by the trial lawyer ally Consumer Federation of California,” Augustine said. “Their misleading attempt to keep this bill from passage before July 1 should be confirmation that our members will be vulnerable to frivolous lawsuits for vehicles that cannot comply with the current deadline.”

SB 719 does not eliminate the protections established by SB 1394. Automakers have already implemented the law’s online process allowing a qualified person to request the termination of another person’s access to connected vehicle services. That protection remains in effect, including the requirement that a completed request be acted upon within two business days.

[IMG:1]

The bill instead revises deadlines for in-vehicle technologies that require extensive engineering, testing and integration across different makes, models, model years and vehicle systems.

## What SB 719 Changes - And What It Preserves

Vehicle development begins seven to eight years before a particular model reaches the road. Changes involving connected services must be engineered and validated to ensure they do not interfere with GPS, theft prevention systems, emergency services, advanced driver assistance systems or other vehicle functions.

Those challenges are particularly significant for existing vehicles. Different makes, models and trim levels use different combinations of hardware and software, and some vehicles cannot receive the required functionality through a software update alone. SB 719 recognizes those technical realities while requiring automakers to implement the protections wherever technologically feasible.

The automotive industry also has supported similar protections at the
federal level
. Alliance for Automotive Innovation supports the bipartisan Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act, introduced by Reps. Debbie Dingell (D-MI) and Dan Crenshaw (R-TX), which would give domestic violence survivors in all states the ability to terminate or disable an abuser’s access to shared connected vehicle services.

SB 719 is currently pending before the Assembly Appropriations Committee and needs to be passed by both the full Assembly and Senate (on concurrence) and signed into law by Gov. Newsom before July 1.

the manufacturers producing most vehicles sold in the U.S. to autonomous vehicle innovators to equipment suppliers, battery producers and semiconductor makers – Alliance for Automotive Innovation represents the full auto industry, a sector supporting 11 million American jobs and more than 5 percent of the economy. queue.title: July 22, 2026 OICA News Olivier FONTAINE, OICA Technical Director, speech at China Auto Forum 2026 Global Harmonisation in a Fragmented World: Despite decades of progress in regulatory harmonisation, new forms of fragmentation are emerging. OICA
queue.text:
## Global Harmonisation in a Fragmented World

The International Organization of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers (OICA) is the global association representing national automotive industry federations, including organisations such as CAAM. Often described as the equivalent of a global federation for the automotive sector, OICA brings together vehicle manufacturers from around the world through their national associations.

OICA currently has 36 member associations across all continents, representing all major vehicle manufacturing regions. The organisation has held official accreditation as a non-governmental organisation at the United Nations since 1956.

[IMG:1]

Approximately 90% of OICA’s activities are focused on automotive regulation at the United Nations. The organisation also publishes global vehicle production statistics, coordinates the international calendar of OICA-accredited motor shows and develops industry position papers, including the OICA Manifesto, through which manufacturers commit to achieving defined levels of vehicle performance.

OICA’s membership includes organisations such as the Alliance for Automotive Innovation in the United States, industry associations from Korea, the SMMT in the United Kingdom and associations from both large and smaller automotive markets. The network continues to expand and now includes most major automotive federations worldwide.

A significant part of OICA’s work takes place within the UNECE World Forum for Harmonization of Vehicle Regulations (WP.29).

[IMG:2]

WP.29 is organised through six specialised subsidiary working groups. OICA has established a technical structure that mirrors this organisation, ensuring that industry expertise is represented across all areas of regulatory development. The OICA Technical Committee reflects the structure of WP.29 and its subsidiary bodies, including GRVA, which is mirrored by OICA’s GEVA working group.

Before each GRX session in Geneva, OICA organises a corresponding preparatory meeting to develop common industry positions. These meetings typically bring together between 15 and 35 experts from around the world. Participation by Japanese and Korean manufacturers has been particularly consistent over many years, allowing them to contribute directly to the development of industry positions that are subsequently discussed within WP.29 and its subsidiary bodies.

This process is open to all manufacturers and associations. Greater participation enables stakeholders to contribute directly to technical discussions and the formulation of industry positions before regulations are finalised.

[IMG:3]

## The Role of the Chinese Automotive Industry in Regulatory Harmonisation

The automotive industry operates on a global scale. Manufacturers seek to market vehicles in China, Europe, the United States, Japan, Korea and many other regions. When each market applies different regulatory requirements, the result is regulatory fragmentation.

Fragmentation creates challenges for Government Authorities, manufacturers and consumers alike.

For national authorities, it increases the burden of assessing vehicle compliance against unique national requirements. For manufacturers, it requires the development of multiple vehicle variants tailored to different regulatory frameworks rather than a single global product. Ultimately, these additional costs are passed on to consumers.

WP.29 was established to address this challenge by providing a platform for the global harmonisation of vehicle regulations.

[IMG:4]

Two principal international agreements form the foundation of this work:

One of the greatest strengths of WP.29 is its role as a neutral platform for regulatory discussion. The process is not political in nature. Regulatory decisions are developed through broad consensus among participants, with the objective of establishing requirements that are acceptable to all contracting parties and that support global market access.

Over time, vehicle performance requirements continue to increase. This evolution is driven by two complementary forces.

The first comes mainly from governments and regulators, whose priorities usually focus on safety, environmental protection and security.

The second comes mainly from industry itself. Technological innovation frequently requires regulatory frameworks to evolve in order to accommodate new products and new forms of mobility.

[IMG:5]

Examples include e-trailers, where regulations are being adapted to allow technologies capable of reducing CO₂ emissions, and Automated Driving Systems (ADS), for which new international regulations have recently been adopted.

In the WP.29 process, Chinese manufacturers have traditionally relied on national authorities to represent their interests. However, participation through OICA provides an additional and highly effective channel for influencing the development of international regulations.

Engagement through OICA allows manufacturers to contribute at an earlier stage of the process, participating directly in the drafting and technical development of regulatory texts.

[IMG:6]

Two conclusions are particularly important.

First, stakeholders that participate in the drafting of international regulations are generally best positioned to influence their content. Rather than simply adapting products to regulatory requirements after they are adopted, manufacturers can contribute to shaping the regulations themselves through active participation in OICA working groups.

Second, seemingly minor technical details can have a significant impact on vehicle design and development. Discussions within OICA frequently address highly specific technical parameters that can ultimately shape future vehicle architectures and technologies. Early involvement therefore offers opportunities to influence issues that may later have important commercial and engineering consequences.

## Global Harmonisation in a Fragmented World

Despite decades of progress in regulatory harmonisation, new forms of fragmentation are emerging.

Two significant drivers of fragmentation are currently shaping the global automotive landscape:

These developments create additional complexity for manufacturers operating internationally.

The challenge is particularly significant because new automotive technologies require scale. Development costs are substantial, and the ability to deploy innovations across multiple markets is often essential to achieving economic viability and delivering benefits to consumers.

[IMG:7]

From a regulatory perspective, WP.29 remains one of the most effective mechanisms for reducing fragmentation and supporting market convergence.

At the same time, the platform itself continues to evolve. Participation from some regions, particularly parts of Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia, remains limited. In addition, many countries apply UN regulations domestically without being formal contracting parties to the principal agreements. Expanding participation remains an important objective.

Within WP.29 and its subsidiary groups, OICA provides technical expertise to support the development of harmonised regulations. Harmonisation helps manufacturers access global markets, reduces administrative burdens for authorities and contributes to high standards of safety, environmental protection and consumer confidence. It also creates opportunities for economies of scale that benefit the entire automotive value chain.

[IMG:8]

To support this objective, OICA actively promotes the benefits of regulatory harmonisation and encourages broader international participation. In recent years, meetings and outreach activities have taken place outside Geneva, including sessions in Bangkok in 2025 and Montréal in 2026. A future WP.29 meeting is planned in Tokyo.

The forthcoming OICA Technical Committee meeting hosted by CAAM in Beijing will provide an additional opportunity for Chinese and other Asian stakeholders to engage directly with OICA activities and international regulatory discussions.

OICA represent the global auto industry that drives economic progress. Through our autos, we connect people, products and services to enhance quality of life and sustainable automobility. We are committed to technological innovation in the areas of safety, environnement, fuel efficiency, and we seek global harmonization of safety and environmental standards to benefit all countries.

The general purposes of the organization are to defend the interests of the vehicle manufacturers, assemblers and importers grouped within their national federation and, in particular :

Link the national automobile associations

Study issues of mutual interest relating to the development and future of the automobile industry

Collect and circulate useful information among member associations

Establish policies and positions on issues of mutual interest to the members

Represent the automobile industry at the international level, in particular with intergovernmental and international bodies

Disseminate and promote industry policies and positions among international bodies and the general public

We are working together around the world.

The organization’s membership comprises 35 trade associations around the world, including all major automobile manufacturing countries, thereby covering virtually the entire motor vehicle industry all over the world.

The organization conducts activities in the fields of technical affairs, communication, and industry statistics. In addition, the Organization Exhibition Committee coordinates international motor shows.

Various committees represent the common interests of automobile industry, and in particular its member associations, at the international level to governments, organizations and to the general public.

At OICA, we do believe in the automobile. It is one of humanity’s most transformative revolutions, unlocking freedom, connection, and progress over the past two centuries.

[IMG:3]

The automobile has empowered people to explore, to bridge cities and nations, and to experience the world in new ways. It has been a driving force for employment, industrial growth, logistics, and relentless innovation in technology and energy.

Just as the United Nations works for peace, we recognize that the pursuit of mobility and progress through the automobile is a universal aspiration, transcending borders, and cultures.

[IMG:4]

We think that science and technology serve people by enabling ever-better vehicles and mobility solutions, aligned with the UN's vision of sustainable, inclusive societies.

Our mission is to support automakers and their automotive associations worldwide, ensuring the continued evolution of cars, trucks, and buses. OICA achieves this through active engagement in regulatory development, the promotion of accurate information, and the global vision of motor shows that celebrate automotive innovation.

OICA’s members are united by a single vision: to build, thanks to automobile, a future where mobility is safer, cleaner, and smarter.

In his new role, he is responsible for the successful further development of the Miba Sinter Group.

Herbert Steiner was born in Salzburg and studied industrial engineering and mechanical engineering at Graz University of Technology. He began his professional career at Audi AG in Ingolstadt in 1998. queue.text:
AISIN‘s “Active Front Spats” Adopted for the First Time on TOYOTA’s New “RAV4” (North American Specification)

The “Active Front Spats” jointly developed by AISIN and TOYOTA, have been adopted for the first time on TOYOTA’s new RAV4 (North American specification). Front spats are installed on the lower section of the front bumper, ahead of the tires, where they optimize airflow around the tires during driving. By reducing aerodynamic drag, they contribute to improved fuel efficiency. Conventional front spats are fixed in position, requiring sufficient ground clearance to avoid contact with the road surface. This constraint has limited their effectiveness in reducing aerodynamic drag. The newly developed and adopted Active Front Spats automatically deploy and retract according to vehicle speed. They retract during standstill and low-speed driving to ensure off-road capability and deploy during high-speed driving through a proprietary link mechanism. This maximizes airflow control around the tires, contributing to improved fuel efficiency and an extended driving range. AISIN is committed to developing technologies that contribute to a better environment and society, in pursuit of its corporate philosophy: Inspiring "movement", creating tomorrow.

queue.title: Jul. 21, 2026 IR AISIN is selected as a constituent of FTSE4Good Index Series, FTSE Blossom Japan Index and FTSE Blossom Japan Sector Relative Index for Consecutive Years
queue.text:
Jul. 21, 2026

AISIN Corporation is selected as a constituent of the FTSE4Good Index Series and FTSE Blossom Japan Index for seven consecutive years, and the FTSE Blossom Japan Sector Relative Index for five consecutive years.

FTSE4Good Index Series
Created by the global index and data provider FTSE Russell, the FTSE4Good Index Series is designed to measure the performance of companies demonstrating strong Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices. The FTSE4Good indexes are used by a wide variety of market participants to create and assess responsible investment funds and other products.
FTSE Russell evaluations are based on performance in areas such as Corporate Governance, Health & Safety, Anti-Corruption and Climate Change.  Businesses included in the FTSE4Good Index Series meet a variety of environmental, social and governance criteria.

FTSE Blossom Japan Index
Created by the global index and data provider FTSE Russell, the FTSE JPX Blossom Japan Index is designed as an industry neutral benchmark that reflects the performance of companies demonstrating specific Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices in Japan.
FTSE Russell evaluations are based on performance in areas such as Corporate Governance, Health & Safety, Anti-Corruption and Climate Change.  Businesses included in the FTSE JPX Blossom Japan Index meet a variety of environmental, social and governance criteria.

FTSE Blossom Japan Sector Relative Index
The FTSE JPX Blossom Japan Sector Relative Index is designed as a sector neutral benchmark that reflects the performance of companies demonstrating specific Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices in Japan. The index selects companies with higher ESG Ratings within the top 50% of each sector and supports climate transition to a low carbon economy by evaluating companies’ climate governance and climate change efforts via the Transition Pathway Initiative’s Management Quality Score.

AISIN will continue to promote the development of technology to improve the environment and society, thereby realizing the AISIN Group Philosophy: Inspiring “movement,” creating tomorrow.
